newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish broker raises year-end ISEQ target to 3,200.
newsitem.headline: Irish broker raises year-end ISEQ target to 3,200.

text.p: The Irish Stock Exchange index, the ISEQ, could appreciate by another nine percent between now and year-end, taking it to 3,200, Davy Stockbrokers said on Monday.
The index has already gained 8.5 percent year-to-date and closed last week at 2,955.91, less than two percent short of Davy's original end-1997 target of 3,000.
The broker expects banking stocks to fuel the rise and is pencilling in a further 15 appreciation for the bank sector between now and year-end.
"On the face of it, the most transparent value in the market still exists in the financial sector," Davy analyst Robbie Kelleher said in a research note.

"In spite of the very significant outperformance since the middle of last year, the bank sector trades on multiples which hardly look stretched -- a price/earnings ratio of 11 times and a yield of 4.3 percent," he said.
Kelleher says an additional 10 percent appreciation would leave the sector multiple at just over 12 times and the yield just below four percent.
This would be in line with current ratings for UK banks but still well below the 13 times rating applying to U.S. banks and the P/E of 14 times given to European banks.
Bank multiples are also well below those of the larger Irish industrials which are on a P/E of 18 times, Kelleher notes.

He says it is difficult to see any significant upside in the larger industrials as the current rating is in line with market averages in the U.S. and Europe and ahead of the average rating for UK industrials which is less than 15 times.
Davy is assuming no more than an average five percent appreciation in the larger industrials this year.

"The best hope in this regard is the paper sector where investors could, later in the year, recognise that the bottom of the price cycle has been passed and the early stages of the next upswing are underway," Davy said.
